Changelog

Source: NEWS.md

cdrgam.cli 0.4.0

  • Lag values accept peak(<term>) and peak-neg(<term>), which hold every term at the lag where the named term’s response is largest or smallest. <term> is a term label from the effect catalog, such as peak(irf(1)).

  • Effects that use a peak write effect-peaks.csv with each peak lag and a level interval from posterior draws of that lag, and the draws in effect-peak-draws.csv. uncertainty.peak_draws sets the number of draws (default 1000; 0 skips them). The draws need cdrgam 0.4.0.

  • Line plots that use a peak can show a timeline of peak lags, intervals, and draws below the main panel. render.peaks is auto (when terms were held at different peak lags), always, or never. The viewer draws the same timeline.

  • cdrgam viz on a root without Slurm, or with --local, prints the viewer’s address and opens the browser; --no-browser suppresses that. A local viewer makes no Slurm calls, so it can run where Slurm does not, such as Windows. --stop and --restart now explain that a local viewer is stopped by interrupting it.

  • Linux hosted checks run on Ubuntu 24.04.

cdrgam.cli 0.3.0

  • Visualization definitions accept preset: irf-lag and preset: irf-predictor. irf-lag plots every ungrouped IRF with one predictor over lag, at the predictor’s mean plus one SD relative to its mean, and can add irf(1). irf-predictor plots the same terms over their predictor values at a fixed lag, 0 by default. Both use simultaneous 95% intervals and a rainbow palette by default, and hold time axes at their training means.

  • Effect-query axis values and references accept arithmetic over an axis’s training mean, sd, and median, such as mean + 2 * sd, and a range: [low, high] grid. Lag values also accept peak (or peak-pos) and peak-neg, the lag at which a term’s response is largest or smallest. A wildcard reference "*" applies to every predictor of each term, and the term selector field interacting keeps or drops terms with more than one predictor.

  • uncertainty: {kind: simultaneous} replaces pointwise limits with simultaneous ones over each term’s grid, computed in the harness from estimate_effect() alone. The viewer offers the same intervals, accepts value expressions in its fixed and reference fields, and now starts unvaried axes at lag 0 and training means rather than medians.

  • Effect queries now hold unspecified time and predictor axes at their training means rather than medians. Grids from existing definitions that relied on the median change.

  • Effects are now evaluated one term at a time. Effect grids gain predictor and predictor_value columns for terms with one predictor, and critical_value for simultaneous intervals. Line renderings accept palette: rainbow and facet scales.

  • Published fit diagnostics include newton_step_max and predicted_decrease_floor from the core, beside predicted_decrease and the raw gradient maxima. A gradient above the tolerance along a well-curved direction can then be read against the negligible Newton step it implies.

  • Rerunning work after its Slurm worker ran out of memory no longer fails at once. The killed worker left its attempt marked running, and when the node reused its process ID for a process the scheduler could not inspect, the attempt was treated as still active, so every new claim failed. An attempt whose Slurm job has ended is now inactive, as is one whose process belongs to another user. When the scheduler fails work without an active attempt, it records the reason on the latest attempt, so status no longer shows the earlier attempt’s error. When squeue no longer knows the job, as happens once Slurm purges a finished job, Slurm accounting decides instead of the recorded process ID.

  • Definitions without fit.rescale_predictors now fit with rescaled predictors, because the core default changed to true. Their model identities and fitted results change accordingly; set fit.rescale_predictors: false to keep native-unit fits.

  • diagnostics.yml now includes the core’s notes, the interior and full outer-Hessian minimum eigenvalues, and one hessian_boundary record per smoothing parameter on the boundary of its range, with its profile bound. These require the development cdrgam that classifies boundary smoothing parameters.

  • Effect visualization queries accept reference, which subtracts the effect at reference axis values, with default leaving a predictor at the model default, and test: true, which writes joint Wald tests to effect-tests.csv. Both require the development cdrgam that provides test_effect(). With composition: total, interaction terms such as irf(wlen, repetition_index, k_p=list(NULL, 3)) now include their lower-order terms, which follows the core change.

  • The deviation composition is removed from visualization queries, layers, and the viewer. It returned the same values as term. Use grouping: deviation for grouped deviations.

  • cdrgam viz has a Reference control. Each line or surface can subtract the effect at reference values of its predictors; an empty field uses the model default. The line label records the reference, and saved lines keep it across reloads.

  • The viewer’s lines pane has a fixed height and scrolls, so the plot keeps its size as lines are added. The pane could previously be pushed out of view.

  • Line renderings draw a separate curve for each value of every varying axis other than x. Several values of a moderator were previously joined into one path. Numeric color and linetype mappings with at most 12 values use a discrete legend.

  • cdrgam purge builds its selection in seconds for projects with many models and datasets. It previously built and renormalized a path for every model and dataset combination against every target, which took more than 25 minutes for a project with 92 models and 65 datasets; it now builds paths only for work directories that exist.

  • Model definitions accept fit.center_predictors (true or false), passed to the core package’s linear-predictor centering.

  • Adds cdrgam viz, a browser viewer for completed fits. It plots effect lines, including several lines from different fits on one plot, and two-axis surfaces, with fixed values for the remaining tensor axes. On Slurm roots the server runs in a per-user Slurm job that later calls reuse. Its Refresh data button picks up new and refitted results, and its Restart server button reloads installed code without a new Slurm job. The viewer’s dependencies (shiny, bslib, plotly, jsonlite, later) are optional.

  • Publishes each finished autosimplification fit to the model’s results directory as it completes. Earlier fits move to model_history/. When no allowed simplification resolves the remaining fit warnings, the last fit stays published with its warnings, status reports an error, and dependent work does not run.

  • Keeps workers connected when the scheduler restarts on the same node. Process start times were stored with about 8 significant digits, so a live scheduler or attempt could look dead and workers ignored the scheduler’s new address. A worker that cannot report a nonconverged or unresolved fit now stops cleanly instead of failing.

cdrgam.cli 0.2.1

  • Repairs release-tag validation for annotated tag messages containing Git’s formatting syntax.

cdrgam.cli 0.2.0

  • Gives clean installations a writable, cross-platform default CDR-GAM root in R’s user data directory. Root-local .cdrgam/site.yml, registry, scheduler state, and projects form one movable harness instance. CDRGAM_ROOT switches that complete instance without splitting configuration from data.
  • Replaces the exported checkout argument with cdrgam_root. Existing sites migrate by placing their scheduler fields and concurrency setting in <CDRGAM_ROOT>/.cdrgam/site.yml and omitting the now-implicit cdrgam_root field.
  • Speeds up work-graph construction by reusing source checksums while file size and modification time are unchanged and by removing redundant filesystem probes from managed-path construction.
  • Reports the current cdrgam run stage on standard error. Interactive terminals receive an in-place, color-rotating activity indicator.
  • Makes purge remove matching artifacts, attempts, logs, and registry records, and strengthens internal module boundaries for focused development tests.

cdrgam.cli 0.1.0

  • Establishes the first public development release of the CDR-GAM project harness.
  • Provides version-controlled project definitions, validation, dependency planning, local execution, and shared Slurm orchestration.
  • Manages atomic artifacts, logs, status, cleanup, publication, and retrieval across projects in one configured harness instance.
